checks.s: The definition retains Corrigan’s carve-out for information independently developed “without reference to” Confidential Information.
The redline deletes or rejects the carve-out for information “generally available within the data analytics industry.”

The definition retains, intact and unaltered, the exclusion for information that “is or becomes generally available to the public other than as a result of a disclosure by the Receiving Party or any of its Representatives in breach of this Agreement.”
The Representatives definition includes affiliates and their respective officers, directors, employees, accountants, counsel, financial advisors, and consultants.
The redline adds language making each party responsible for breaches by its Representatives, including affiliates.
The Permitted Purpose is “evaluating a potential acquisition by Velantis of the Data Analytics Division of Corrigan,” or uses substantively identical language.
The confidentiality term is 2 years from the date of the agreement.
The redline restores a residuals clause allowing the Receiving Party to use “residual knowledge” retained in the unaided memory of its personnel.
The residuals clause excludes trade secrets and information identified in writing as “Highly Confidential — No Residuals.”
The redline deletes or rejects Corrigan’s “highest degree of care” standard.

The redline restores a standard substantially equivalent to “reasonable care, and in no event less than the same degree of care the Receiving Party uses to protect its own confidential information of a similar nature.”
The redline deletes or rejects language requiring the Disclosing Party to bear all costs of seeking a protective order.
The redline provides that each party bears its own costs and that the Receiving Party uses commercially reasonable efforts to cooperate, or uses substantially equivalent language.
The return/destruction window is 10 business days.
The redline adds a carve-out for electronically archived copies retained under bona fide document-retention policies and keeps those copies subject to confidentiality obligations.
The non-solicitation period is 18 months.
The redline deletes Corrigan’s $150,000 liquidated damages provision.
The redline provides equitable relief, including an injunction, as a remedy for a non-solicitation breach.
The redline retains any standstill or don't-ask-don't-waive (DADW) language.

The cover note presents a 6-month standstill with a fall-away upon any third-party bid and no don't-ask-don't-waive (DADW) provision as a negotiating concession only if Corrigan insists on a standstill.
The redline restores Delaware as the governing law and rejects Corrigan’s change to Virginia.
The redline deletes or rejects binding JAMS arbitration in Richmond, Virginia.
The redline restores exclusive jurisdiction in the Delaware Court of Chancery or, if unavailable, the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware.
The redline retains or includes language stating that neither party is obligated to consummate a transaction.
The redline deletes or rejects Corrigan’s language stating there is no obligation to continue discussions or negotiate in good faith.
The redline includes “Nothing herein shall obligate either party to consummate any transaction,” or substantively equivalent language.
The redline rejects the $500,000 bond requirement and provides for injunctive relief “without bond” or “without the necessity of posting bond.”
The cover note is from David Orenbach of Kirkner Pratt LLP.
The cover note is addressed to Nina Vasquez of Threlkeld & Aaronson PLLC.
The cover note’s cc line includes both Rachel Sung and Marcus Leeland.
The cover note addresses all 14 substantive changes in the Corrigan markup and distinguishes which changes are accepted, partially accepted, and rejected.
The cover note identifies May 30, 2025, as the target NDA execution date.
The cover note identifies June 2, 2025, as the diligence commencement date.
The cover note uses the May 30 execution date and June 2 diligence date to communicate urgency for a prompt response.
The counter-turn redline uses the project code name “Project Lantern” consistently throughout.
The redline identifies “Velantis Technologies, Inc.” as a Delaware corporation.
The redline identifies “Corrigan Systems Group, LLC” as a Virginia limited liability company.
The cover note explains that the standstill is inappropriate for a consensual, buy-side-initiated process.
The cover note presents a 6-month standstill, a fall-away upon a third-party bid, and no DADW as a fallback concession available only if Corrigan insists, not as an affirmative offer.
The deliverable is structured or described as a Microsoft Word Track Changes document against Corrigan’s first markup, “corrigan-first-markup-nda.docx,” showing Velantis’s counter-positions.
The cover note explains that “highest degree of care” is above market standard and that “reasonable care / no less than own standard” is appropriate for M&A NDAs.
The cover note explains that “without bond” is standard for M&A NDAs or consistent with Delaware Court of Chancery practice as the reason for rejecting the $500,000 bond requirement.

The cover note addresses customer lists, proprietary algorithms, and employee compensation data, and explains that the qualified residuals clause and confidentiality obligations adequately address those concerns.
The cover note identifies the residuals clause’s exclusions for trade secrets and information marked “Highly Confidential — No Residuals.”
The cover note explains that injunctive relief provisions are better served by court jurisdiction in the Delaware Court of Chancery than by JAMS arbitration in Richmond, Virginia.
The cover note mentions or discloses the estimated enterprise value of Corrigan DAD as $215 million.
The cover note mentions or discloses an implied revenue figure of $43 million for Corrigan DAD.
The cover note names Haldane Ridgeway & Co. as Velantis’s financial advisor.
The cover note states that the Corrigan markup contains 14 substantive changes or addresses exactly 14 substantive items.
The cover note or redline states that the Corrigan markup contains approximately six (6) conforming or typographical edits, or six such edits, and acknowledges that they are accepted.
The counter-turn redline accepts, without rejecting or modifying, the 6 conforming or typographical edits from Corrigan’s markup.
